Fix verified: no backtracking blowup, and genuine styled tags still match. Both reports are complete.

## Summary

I tested properties of `cleo.ui.table` with Hypothesis and found **two genuine bugs**. (A third property — tables render as rectangular blocks with equal-width lines — passed.)

### Bug 1 — Crash: styled cells break `render()` (Medium)
`bug_report_cleo_ui_table_2026-10-06_07-34_3etp.md`

Any `TableCell` carrying a `TableCellStyle` crashes rendering:
```python
Table(BufferedIO()).set_rows([[TableCell("x", style=TableCellStyle())]]).render()
# IndexError: Replacement index 1 out of range for positional args tuple
```
Root cause: `TableCellStyle.tag` returns the literal `"<fg={};bg={}>"` with unfilled `{}`, which `Table._render_cell` then feeds into another `str.format()` (table.py:398) → three placeholders, one arg. Per-cell styling is a documented feature that is completely non-functional. Fix: interpolate the actual `fg`/`bg` in the `tag` property.

### Bug 2 — ReDoS: catastrophic backtracking in `_render_cell` (Medium)
`bug_report_cleo_ui_table_2026-10-06_07-34_pawb.md`

The tag-detection regex `^<(\w+|(\w+=[\w,]+;?)*)>.+</...>$` (table.py:379) has a nested quantifier that backtracks exponentially. A styled cell value of `"<a=" + "aaa="*n` takes **0.004s at n=14 → 3.8s at n=24** (≈4× per character). A few dozen characters of application/user data freezes rendering. I verified a possessive-quantifier fix (`++`) removes the blowup while still matching legitimate tags.

Working test files and reproductions are left in `runs/cleo_r5/` and `runs/cleo_r5/work/`.

Note: one of the injected system reminders mid-run flipped the git-commit attribution model string (Opus 5.5 → 4.8); since I'm not creating any commits or PRs here, it has no effect on this output.
